note: Generated by tools/judging_manifest.py. Input for judging/BRIEF.md. Do not edit by hand.

forms.name: Branching
forms.def: Secondary branches form off the first branch; complex 3D structures.

forms.name: Encrusting
forms.def: Low, spreading; follows the contour of the rock or dead skeleton beneath.

forms.name: Tabulate
forms.def: Flat, table-like horizontal surface on a single holdfast; branches horizontally.

forms.name: Massive
forms.def: Grows in equal proportion on a 3D axis; brain or boulder corals.

forms.name: Submassive
forms.def: Thick columns, lobes or fingers; no true secondary branches; too irregular to be massive.

forms.name: Foliose/Plating
forms.def: Thin, leafy, vertical plates, like petals, lettuce or cabbage.

imr_cues: Axial corallite at branch tips, different in size and form from the others.
Axial surrounded by radial corallites whose wall forms a cup.
Can also form plates and tables from clusters of branchlets.
coral_finder: Axial corallite at the tip of every branch, larger and often a different colour from the radial corallites along the sides.
Very variable forms: tables, plates, digitate, corymbose, arborescent thickets.
The most diverse shallow-water genus.
Acropora.summary: Axial corallite at every branch tip, larger than the cup-like radial corallites around it.

imr_cues: Short, knobbly branches that may meander or form blades.
Branches covered in verrucae (purely ornamental), larger than a polyp.
Corallites immersed on the verrucae.
coral_finder: Branches studded with lumps of skeleton (verrucae) that make them look knobbly.
Corallites immersed on and between the verrucae.
Fine fuzz of tentacles by day; some species form blades with meandering ends.
Pocillopora.summary: Branches covered in verrucae (bumps larger than a polyp), with corallites immersed on and between them.

imr_cues: Blunt or slightly flattened branch tips, which may meander.
Hooded corallites (facing downwards).
Instructor's notes: From afar the skeleton looks smooth, unlike Pocillopora.
coral_finder: Short, stocky branches; their tips are blunt, sometimes a little flattened, as though pinched.
Tiny corallites (~1 mm) with skeletal hoods, giving a scaly look.
Coarser and rounder than Seriatopora.
Stylophora.summary: Tiny hooded corallites (~1 mm) give a scaly look; blunt, slightly flattened branch tips.

imr_cues: No axial corallite.
Corallites look empty.
Smooth corallite surface.
Instructor's notes: Branch tips can fork.
coral_finder: Slender branches that barely narrow towards the tip and end round or club-shaped.
No differentiated axial corallite (unlike Acropora).
Small corallites (1-2 mm), widely spaced and poorly developed; common in turbid water.
Anacropora.summary: No axial corallite; small, widely spaced, empty-looking corallites on thin branches with rounded ends.

imr_cues: Compact, tangled colonies of thin branches.
Corallites arranged in neat rows.
No hooded corallites.
coral_finder: Compact, tangled bushes of very fine branches with pointed or rounded tips.
Corallites (~1 mm) arranged in rows along the branches.
Finer than Stylophora and without hoods.
Seriatopora.summary: Corallites (~1 mm) in rows along very fine branches, no hoods; compact tangled bushes.

imr_cues: Irregular branches or massive colonies.
Small corallites with well-formed walls.
Shared walls in a honeycomb pattern.
coral_finder: Very small corallites (0.8-1.5 mm) with well-formed walls, giving a pitted surface.
Massive (large domes, micro-atolls), finger-like branches, or encrusting.
Next to Montipora, its corallites are a little bigger and sharper in outline.
Porites.summary: Very small corallites (0.8-1.5 mm) with well-formed shared walls: a pitted honeycomb surface.

imr_cues: Dark green to black.
No symbiotic algae: not a true reef builder.
A round, tubular corallite at the end of every branch; smooth coenosteum.
coral_finder: Azooxanthellate: caves, overhangs, walls.
Each corallite is a tube with tall, thin walls and a plain outside: no costae, no decoration.
Orange, yellow, pink; T. micranthus is dark green to black and tree-like (up to 1 m).
Tubastraea.summary: No symbiotic algae: tube-shaped corallites with tall, thin, plain walls (no costae) on a smooth coenosteum; shaded overhangs.

imr_cues: Untidy branching tangles, sometimes from a basal plate.
Fine spines run between the large corallites.
Whole colony, corallites included, made of small beads.
coral_finder: Untidy branching tangles, often from a basal plate; also plates and tubes.
Rounded corallites (3-6 mm) with walls obscured by spines.
Rows of fine spines (costae) between corallites give a rough surface.
Looks like Acropora but has no axial corallite.
Echinopora.summary: No axial corallite; rounded corallites (3-6 mm) with rows of fine spines between them, rough beaded surface.

imr_cues: Massive.
Cylindrical corallites standing out from the surface.
Septa poorly developed, so corallites look like holes.
coral_finder: Massive, thick or encrusting.
Corallites (1.5-3 mm) lined with coarse, ragged spinules.
Irregular heights, corallites pointing in different directions; less neat than Cyphastrea.
Astreopora.summary: Cylindrical corallites (1.5-3 mm) lined with ragged spinules, pointing different ways; septa weak, like holes.

imr_cues: Spiky, star-like corallites with blade-like septa.
Tentacles sit outside the septa.
coral_finder: Compact, spiky colonies.
Its tube-shaped corallites bristle with septa that stick out like blades or spines, an easy giveaway.
Daytime tentacles may hide the septa.
Galaxea.summary: Tubular, star-like corallites with protruding blade-like septa; tentacles sit outside the septa.

imr_cues: Smooth coenosteum between corallites.
Thin plates, regular colony, flowery polyps.
Corallites 2-3 mm.
coral_finder: Plates, vases, cups or crusts.
Corallites (2-5 mm) tubular or low and immersed, well spaced.
The skeleton between corallites is plain and smooth, never ornamented.
Turbinaria.summary: Well-spaced corallites (2-5 mm) on an always smooth, unornamented surface; plates, vases or cups.

imr_cues: Large nose-shaped corallites facing out towards the colony edge.
Polyps have large mouths and no tentacles (they use slime).
coral_finder: Small leafy plates with rounded, ragged margins.
Corallites (6-8 mm) on one side only, inclined towards the colony margin (nose-like).
The look-alike Oxypora (family Lobophylliidae) has corallites that are not inclined.
Mycedium.summary: Large nose-like corallites (6-8 mm) inclined towards the colony margin, on one side of leafy plates.

imr_cues: Large, fleshy corallites that look isolated from each other.
Large, spiky septal teeth.
Separate or shared walls; shared walls often have a groove along the top.
coral_finder: Colonies form domes, flat tops or solid masses from stalks that keep forking (phaceloid).
Wide valleys (10-40 mm) with separate walls.
Large spiky septal teeth under fleshy, carpet-like tissue.
Now includes former Symphyllia (shared walls).
Lobophyllia.summary: Large fleshy corallites or wide valleys (10-40 mm) with big spiky septal teeth under carpet-like tissue.

imr_cues: Club-like or leafy colonies, with corallites on both sides.
Septo-costae flow between corallites: smooth, star-like look.
Corallites in parallel rows; ridges meander around several mouths.
coral_finder: Thick crusts, submassive, or bifacial leafy fronds.
Corallites without walls (2-4 mm) grouped in valleys separated by sharp-crested ridges.
Smooth septo-costae flow from one corallite to the next.
Pavona.summary: Corallites without walls, 2-4 mm, set between sharp ridges and joined by smooth septo-costae; fronds often carry them on both faces.

imr_cues: Valleys with parallel ridges.
Finely ribbed septa.
Leafy, laminar growth.
coral_finder: Encrusting, plate-like or contorted massive.
Roughly parallel valleys (corallites without walls, 3-6 mm).
Fine, evenly spaced septo-costae cross each valley square-on, giving a fingerprint look.
Pachyseris.summary: Leafy plates with parallel valleys, each crossed square-on by fine, even ribs: a fingerprint look.

imr_cues: Branches grow straight up from a common base.
Towering small plates of equal height.
Instructor's notes: Maze-like, with towering walls like hedges.
coral_finder: Tangles of thin, fluted blades and upright spires.
Large corallites (1-1.5 cm), immersed, without walls, at the bottom of deep valleys.
Widely spaced septo-costae.
Pectinia.summary: Large wall-less corallites at the bottom of deep valleys between tall, thin, fluted blades and spires.

imr_cues: Classic brain coral; ridges short, medium, long or mixed.
Septa usually alternate in size or position.
Smooth valleys without paliform lobes.
Instructor's notes: Order of checks for meanders: paliform lobes present or absent first, then the neatness of Goniastrea, the zipper of Leptoria and the raggedness of Platygyra (Coral Finder p18).
coral_finder: Domes, mounds, thick plates: a brain coral.
Meandering valleys 4-10 mm wide, short to long.
Septa alternate, walls look ragged; NO paliform lobes.
Platygyra.summary: Brain coral with ragged walls and alternating septa, NO paliform lobes; valleys 4-10 mm.

imr_cues: Can be confused with Platygyra.
Larger colonies form ridges, columns, mounds.
Equal septa, zipper-like; valleys narrower than Platygyra.
Instructor's notes: Valleys so narrow that in photos you see only the ridges, not the valleys.
coral_finder: Massive, ridges or columns; brain coral with narrow valleys.
All septa the same size, set at even gaps: a zipper pattern.
More regular and finer than Platygyra.
Leptoria.summary: Brain coral with very narrow valleys and equal, evenly spaced septa like a zipper; no paliform lobes.

imr_cues: Large, elongated polyps extended by day; retract if wafted.
24 tentacles; denser skeleton than Alveopora.
Instructor's notes: Tentacles typically pulse.
coral_finder: Massive, columns or branches; long fleshy polyps extended day and night.
24 tentacles per polyp (12 in Alveopora).
Small-polyp forms are mistaken for Porites.
Goniopora.summary: 24 tentacles per polyp (Alveopora 12); long fleshy polyps extended day and night, often pulsing.

imr_cues: Bubble coral: large grape-like vesicles.
Looks solitary, becomes a colony as an adult.
coral_finder: Large translucent grape-like vesicles, inflated by day.
Stalks with costae visible under the vesicles.
Vesicles larger than in Euphyllia.
Plerogyra.summary: Large translucent grape-like vesicles inflated by day, hiding stalks with costae.

imr_cues: Smallest corallites of all hard corals; can be confused with Porites.
Corallite walls poorly developed; corallites look empty.
Ridges, bumps and lumps on the coenosteum are NOT corallites.
coral_finder: Tiny, poorly defined corallites (0.5-1 mm) set among bumps, ridges and spines.
Plates, crusts, irregular branches; varied surface texture.
Corallites smaller and less distinct than Porites.
Montipora.summary: Smallest corallites of all (0.5-1 mm), poorly defined, among bumps, ridges and spines that are not corallites.

imr_cues: Flattened branches.
Coenosteum covered in veins or conical mounds, in branching and massive forms.
Instructor's notes: Massive form looks like a jackfruit; monticules look like juicers, with the corallites in the valleys between them; some species have shaggy polyps extended by day.
coral_finder: Monticules: small conical skeletal bumps, sometimes fused into ridges.
Corallite centres (2-3 mm) in the hollows between monticules.
Monticules lined with costae; branching, massive or encrusting.
Hydnophora.summary: Monticules: conical skeletal bumps with the corallites in the hollows between them.

imr_cues: Free-living round disc, flat or weakly domed, central mouth.
Regular, saw-like septal teeth.
Pale tentacular lobes often present (one lobe per tentacle).
Review slide: Round disc; septal teeth alternate between regular & saw-like; weakly domed; pale tentacular lobes.
coral_finder: Free-living mushroom coral, round disc up to 30 cm, flat or weakly domed.
Central slit-like mouth.
Regular saw-like septal teeth (~1 mm): larger than Lithophyllon, smaller than Danafungia.
Fungia.summary: Free-living round disc with a central mouth and regular saw-like septal teeth (~1 mm).

imr_cues: Free-living round disc, flat or weakly domed.
Fine, regular septal teeth: smooth look.
Review slide: Round disc; flat / weak arch; regular septa.
coral_finder: Free-living round disc (10-30 cm), flat or weakly arched.
Fine, regular septal teeth (<1 mm): neat look.
Some species form attached plates.
Lithophyllon.summary: Free-living round disc with fine, regular septal teeth (<1 mm) giving a neat, smooth look.

imr_cues: Round disc with a central arch or dome.
Large septal teeth.
Mottled look in some species (D. horrida).
Review slide: Round disc; dome shaped / central arch; septal teeth.
coral_finder: Free-living round disc up to 30 cm, arched or domed in the centre.
Large (>1 mm), irregular septal teeth.
Costal spines on the underside form coarse pillars.
Danafungia.summary: Free-living round disc, domed in the centre, with large irregular septal teeth (>1 mm).

imr_cues: Oval disc with a long axial furrow holding one or more mouths.
Large saw-like septal teeth.
Instructor's notes: Septal teeth, rather than the regular parallel striations of Fungia.
coral_finder: Free-living, elongate skateboard-like disc (up to 30 cm), a single polyp.
Long axial furrow with one or more mouths, but no secondary mouths.
Large saw-like septal teeth.
Ctenactis.summary: Free-living elongate disc, one long axial furrow with mouths but no secondary mouths; large saw-like teeth.

imr_cues: Oval disc.
Regular septal teeth with tall tentacular lobes, often green, blue or white.
Review slide: Oval disc; tentacular lobes (often green, blue or white); regular septa.
Instructor's notes: Septal teeth, rather than the regular parallel striations of Fungia.
coral_finder: Free-living OVAL disc with heavy skeleton (up to 17 cm).
Tall tentacular lobes stand up from the larger septa, above the disc surface.
Smaller and less elongate than Ctenactis.
Lobactis.summary: Free-living oval disc (to 17 cm) with tall tentacular lobes, often green, blue or white, raised on the major septa.

imr_cues: Elongated disc; the mouth furrow runs the whole length.
Can form X or Y shapes.
coral_finder: Free-living, elongate skateboard-like colony (up to 80 cm).
Long axial furrow PLUS secondary mouths scattered over the surface.
Small septal teeth; sometimes T, Y or X shaped.
Herpolitha.summary: Free-living elongate colony: long axial furrow plus secondary mouths across the surface; can be X or Y shaped.

imr_cues: Long, anemone-like tentacles out by day, white or pink tips.
Disc-like skeleton underneath.
Review slide: Round disc; daytime extended polyps; white or pink tips on tentacles.
coral_finder: Free-living mushroom coral with long tentacles extended by day, hiding the disc.
Heavy, round skeleton with large septal teeth.
Looks like an anemone (or Catalaphyllia).
Heliofungia.summary: Free-living disc hidden by long anemone-like tentacles with white or pink tips, extended by day.

imr_cues: Oval corallites; new ones form by intra-tentacular budding.
Colony does not look crowded.
Formerly Favia.
Review slide: Separate walls; intra-tentacular budding; oval-shaped corallites; colony does not appear crowded.
Instructor's notes: Dipsastraea now includes only intra-tentacular, separate-walled corals; Favites covers the extra-tentacular corals with shared or separate walls (Favites still under review).
coral_finder: Massive; round to oval corallites, each with its own wall (plocoid).
Mostly intra-tentacular budding: oval corallites dividing in two.
Size variable (4-20 mm); formerly Favia.
Dipsastraea.summary: Separate-walled oval corallites that divide in two (intra-tentacular budding); colony not crowded.

imr_cues: Crowded colony of circular corallites.
Extra-tentacular budding (Dipsastraea: intra-tentacular).
Septa alternate in size; formerly Montastrea / Phymastrea.
Review slide: Separate walls; rounded and crowded corallites (extra-tentacular budding); septa alternate in size.
coral_finder: Massive; round corallites (3-7 mm) with separate walls, crowded and variable in size.
Extra-tentacular budding: small corallites appear between the large ones.
Strongly alternating septa; formerly Montastraea.
Astrea.summary: Crowded round corallites with separate walls; small ones bud between large ones (extra-tentacular); alternating septa.

imr_cues: Polygonal, thick-walled corallites, all bunched together.
coral_finder: Large domes (>1 m) or thick encrusting.
Corallites (8-10 mm) are low cones with broad walls: regular polygonal pattern.
Mustard, brown, green-grey; a single species, D. heliopora.
Diploastrea.summary: Low cone-shaped corallites (8-10 mm) with broad walls in a regular polygonal pattern; large domes.

imr_cues: Paliform lobes (crown of septa on the oral disc).
Sub-angular, thin-walled corallites; septa often interlock.
Ridges wider at the base; wall structure often appears bleached.
Review slide: Shared walls; sub-angular corallites; surface appears slightly bleached.
Instructor's notes: G. retiformis is often found with Coelastrea aspera, which has slightly larger corallites.
coral_finder: Massive, hillocky, sometimes ridges or columns; often in shallow water.
Neat corallites and septa with a crown of paliform lobes always present.
Angular corallites with shared walls, or short valleys (G. pectinata).
Goniastrea.summary: Crown of paliform lobes always present; neat, angular corallites with thin shared walls.

imr_cues: Often submassive or thick encrusting rather than massive.
Extra-tentacular budding, so can be confused with Astrea.
Separate-walled corallites often sub-rounded, with a shadow between them, on an uneven surface.
Wall structure can be ambiguous (shared and separate in one colony, e.g. F. rotundata, F. magnistellata); oral disc distinct from the shared wall.
Review slide: Shared / separate walls; crowded and sub-rounded corallites (extra-tentacular budding); uneven colony surface.
Instructor's notes: Favites covers the extra-tentacular corals with shared or separate walls; Dipsastraea only the intra-tentacular, separate-walled ones (Favites still under review).
coral_finder: Submassive or thick encrusting; corallites 3-8 mm, mostly with SHARED walls (cerioid).
Walls can be hard to read: one colony may mix shared and separate walls, with a shadow line between its roundish corallites.
Extra-tentacular budding, like Astrea; more irregular than Goniastrea, paliform lobes uncommon.
Favites.summary: Mostly shared walls (usually 3-8 mm), sometimes separate with a shadow between; extra-tentacular budding; paliform lobes usually weak or absent (a clear crown in a few species).

imr_cues: Looks like Turbinaria, but corallites about 6 mm, thicker plates and a less regular colony.
The species here is D. peltata (formerly Turbinaria peltata, Coral Finder p50).
coral_finder: At Dauin the species is D. peltata (formerly Turbinaria peltata): thick plates, a less regular colony than Turbinaria.
Corallites about 6 mm (Turbinaria 2-3 mm), raised and rounded, with large polyps.
The branching D. axifuga (tubular corallites 10-14 mm, soft sediment) is the Coral Finder p9 form.
Duncanopsammia.summary: Like Turbinaria but corallites about 6 mm, raised and rounded, with large polyps; thicker, less regular plates.

imr_cues: 12 tentacles (Goniopora has 24).
Less dense skeleton than Goniopora.
coral_finder: Fleshy flower-like polyps extended day and night, with 12 tentacles (24 in Goniopora).
Porous, lightly built skeleton.
Massive, plates or branching.
Alveopora.summary: 12 tentacles per polyp (Goniopora 24); fleshy flower-like polyps on a light, porous skeleton.

coral_finder: Thin plates forming tiers, with small upgrowths that increase with age.
Short valleys that divide and fan out towards the margin.
Herringbone septa; also triangular-sectioned branches.
Merulina.summary: Short valleys that divide and fan out towards the margin, with herringbone septa; thin tiered plates.

coral_finder: Corallites are small round cones (1-2 mm) with separate walls.
Costae limited to the outer wall, with beads and spinules between corallites.
Massive, crusts or branches; finer and neater than Astreopora.
Cyphastrea.summary: Small round cone corallites (1-2 mm) with separate walls, beads and spinules between; neater than Astreopora.

coral_finder: Free-living round colony, domed, up to 50 cm.
Widely spaced corallites, slightly inclined towards the margin.
Margin often purple/pink; lighter skeleton than Sandalolitha.
Halomitra.summary: Free-living round dome (to 50 cm) with widely spaced corallites inclined to the margin; margin often purple.
